skill.name: Writing Hookify Rules
skill.description: Guides users through writing Hookify rules that watch tool activity, match patterns, and show warnings or blocks in Claude workflows.
skill.summary: Create Hookify rule files with event types, regex patterns, conditions, messages, and workflow guidance.
skill.author: anthropics

content.value_statement: Hook rules can be hard to write because events, fields, and regex syntax must align. This skill gives clear templates and examples for building Hookify rules for Claude workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Hookify Markdown rule structure with YAML frontmatter.
Defines bash, file, stop, prompt, and all event types.
Shows simple pattern rules and multi-condition rules.
Provides regex tips for escaping and matching common patterns.
Describes file naming, location, and gitignore practices.
Lists example rule ideas for dangerous commands and sensitive file edits.
limitations: Does not install, run, or validate Hookify itself.
Does not replace security review of generated rules.
Examples are guidance and may need project-specific adjustment.
Does not include a test harness beyond a simple regex command example.

use_cases.title: Add command safeguards
use_cases.description: Create Hookify rules that warn or block risky shell commands before they run.

use_cases.title: Warn on sensitive edits
use_cases.description: Draft file rules that detect edits involving environment files, credentials, or generated folders.

use_cases.title: Enforce completion checks
use_cases.description: Build stop-event reminders that ask agents to verify tests, builds, and documentation before finishing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Bash Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns when Claude runs a command matching [pattern]. Include the event, pattern, and warning message.

prompt_templates.title: Build a File Edit Warning
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify file rule that checks [file type] edits for [pattern]. Explain each frontmatter field in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Add Multiple Conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Hookify rule with conditions for file path and new text. Use [path pattern] and [text pattern], then explain testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Rule Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three Hookify rules for [workflow]. Cover bash, file, and stop events, with names, actions, patterns, and messages.

output_examples.input: Create a warning for recursive removal commands.
output_examples.output: A bash-event rule plan with a recursive removal pattern, a clear warning, and safer command alternatives.

output_examples.input: Warn when environment files receive API key text.
output_examples.output: A multi-condition file rule concept that checks file path and added text, plus a message about gitignore and secret handling.

output_examples.input: Remind the agent to run tests before stopping.
output_examples.output: A stop-event checklist reminder that asks for test, build, and documentation verification before completion.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the risky behavior without blocking unrelated work.
Write messages that explain the risk and suggest a safer next step.
Store local rules in the documented .claude location and keep them out of commits when appropriate.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match common words across unrelated commands or files.
Do not rely on warnings alone for actions that require enforcement.
Do not copy example patterns without testing them against project-specific commands and files.

faq.question: Does this skill run Hookify rules?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for writing rule files. Hookify handles rule loading and enforcement.

faq.question: Can it create rules for Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains rule patterns that can support Claude Code workflows when Hookify is available.

faq.question: Does it require advanced regex knowledge?
faq.answer: No. It explains basic regex syntax, escaping rules, and common matching mistakes.

faq.question: Can rules block dangerous commands?
faq.answer: The skill can help draft rules with a block action. Hookify decides how that action is enforced.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple matching conditions?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents condition lists for matching fields such as command, file path, and new text.

faq.question: Will it protect secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can help create warnings for secret-like edits, but teams still need proper secret management.
